_meta.status: LIVE on main -- all 51 states + DC published (batch 4, 2026-07-25)
_meta.purpose: Per-state CPA license reinstatement cost + penalty-CPE data: what a lapsed CPA actually owes to get reinstated (fee + catch-up CPE hours + ethics hours), sourced fresh -- this dataset did not exist anywhere on the site before 2026-07-25. Same 2-source verification standard as cpa_deadlines.json and cpe_hours.json: a board page + a codified rule/statute for every record. Genuinely empty shelf per ScoutLab's 2026-07-21 product register (no per-state reinstatement calculator exists anywhere) -- built as the free lead-magnet the affiliate-only monetization pivot recommended, not a paid SKU.
_meta.publish_rule: 2-source standard: board page + codified rule/statute for every record. A state whose real-world fee/hours figure is a formula (not a flat number) reports null in the numeric field and explains the formula in the matching *_notes field and data_gap_note -- never a guessed point figure.
_meta.does_not_touch: cpa_deadlines.json / cpe_hours.json unchanged -- this is a new, independent dataset.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Not a flat fee. Code of Ala. 1975 §34-1-11(d) lets the Board set a reinstatement fee (not exceeding $100) plus back registration fees and late penalties for every lapsed year -- the Board's own fee schedule sets the annual permit fee at $100 (individual)/$130 (firm) and late penalties of $100 (if filed Jan1-Feb28/29) or $500 (if filed after), compounding per lapsed year.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: Formula: Ala. Admin. Code r. 30-X-5-.02(3)-(4) requires 40 CPE hours for EACH year off active status, capped at 120 hours (3+ lapsed years), with 20% in accounting & auditing, earned within the 3 years preceding the request.
records.lapse_trigger: Annual permits expire September 30; renewal (application, fee, CPE proof) is due by December 31. A $100 late penalty applies if filed Jan 1-Feb 28/29, a $500 late penalty if filed Mar 1-31. Failing to renew or apply for inactive status within 6 months of expiration (roughly by the following March 31) is itself grounds for revocation under Code of Ala. §34-1-11(d), after which formal reinstatement (a Board hearing) plus back-fees and catch-up CPE apply.
records.citation: Code of Alabama 1975, §34-1-11(d) (reinstatement fee & lapse/revocation trigger); Ala. Admin. Code r. 30-X-3-.07 (annual permit fees & late penalties); Ala. Admin. Code r. 30-X-5-.02(3)-(4) (catch-up CPE hours)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: $300 biennial renewal fee (12 AAC 02.340(4)) plus $100 delayed-renewal penalty (12 AAC 02.340(13)), once a license has lapsed more than 60 days -- covers the common under-1-year lapse. For a longer lapse (1-3 years), the $300 renewal fee is owed for EACH lapsed biennial period, so the total scales up; a lapse of 5+ years cannot be reinstated at all.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: For a lapse of 1+ years: 120 hours of approved CE completed in the 36 months preceding the reinstatement application (vs. the normal 80 hours/2 years) -- no more than 16 of those hours may be micro-learning. A lapse under 1 year requires no extra CE beyond normal compliance.
records.lapse_trigger: Licenses are biennial, expiring December 31 of odd-numbered years regardless of issuance date. Missing that deadline lapses the license immediately; a $100 delayed-renewal penalty attaches once the lapse exceeds 60 days.
records.citation: 12 AAC 04.440(a)-(f) (Reinstatement of Lapsed License); fee amounts at 12 AAC 02.340(4),(12),(13); license-term backdrop at 12 AAC 04.189

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Same $100 application fee as new certification (Ariz. Admin. Code R4-1-341(A)(1)). Once reinstatement from canceled status is approved, the standard biennial registration fee ($100-$300, prorated) also applies -- total out-of-pocket can exceed $100.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: Not a punitive add-on: up to 160 hours of CPE in the 4 years immediately before reinstating (R4-1-453(C)(7)) -- the same cumulative total a continuously-registered CPA owes over 4 years, capped even if the lapse ran longer.
records.lapse_trigger: Individual registration is biennial, keyed to the registrant's birth month with odd/even-year parity (R4-1-345). Missing the birth-month renewal deadline draws a $50 late fee; if still unrenewed, the certificate lapses to 'canceled' status, requiring reinstatement under A.R.S. §32-732(B). If 25-48 months have passed since the last renewal due date, the ethics-hour requirement doubles to 8 hours (vs. the normal 4).
records.citation: Ariz. Admin. Code R4-1-341(A)(1) (reinstatement fee); R4-1-453(C)(4),(7) (normal vs. reinstatement CPE/ethics hours); A.R.S. §32-732(B) (reinstatement from canceled status); R4-1-345(B)-(C) (birth-year-parity cycle)
records.data_gap_note: The Board's own reinstatement page (azaccountancy.gov) could not be reached directly at publish time. The $100 fee and CPE/ethics-hour figures above come from the codified rule cited here (Ariz. Admin. Code R4-1-341, R4-1-453), which is authoritative on its own, and the same $100 fee also appears on an archived copy of the Board's page.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Flat, non-refundable $150 reinstatement fee (Board Rule 12.2) if reinstated within 3 years of expiration -- distinct from the separate $25/month late-renewal fee that accrues in the first 3 months after the December 31 expiration, before the license actually lapses.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: No extra CPE beyond the standard renewal formula for a sub-3-year lapse: 40 hours of CPE for each consecutive 12-month period lapsed (pro-rated at 3 1/3 hours/month), the same rate as ordinary renewal -- not an add-on penalty.
records.lapse_trigger: Licenses expire annually on December 31. A monthly late fee accrues starting January 1; if still not renewed by April 1 of the following year, the license automatically LAPSES by operation of statute.
records.citation: Ark. Code Ann. §17-12-504(f)-(h) (late fee, lapse trigger, 3-year reinstatement window); Arkansas State Board of Public Accountancy Rule 12.2 (reinstatement fee) and Rule 13.7(d)/13.9 (CPE required for reinstatement)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: California calls this the 'delinquency fee,' not a separate line item -- $200 for a license expiring after June 30, 2026 ($170 before), equal to 50% of the $400/$340 renewal fee (Bus. & Prof. Code §163.5).
records.penalty_cpe_notes: Formula: an additional 20 hours of CE for each full 6-month period between expiration and the renewal application date, capped at 80 additional hours on top of the normal 80-hour/2-year requirement. No extra CE if less than 6 full months have elapsed.
records.lapse_trigger: An individual permit expires at the end of the second year of a 2-year cycle anchored to the licensee's own birth month (Bus. & Prof. Code §5070.5). A delinquent (expired) permit may still be renewed for up to 5 years after expiration by paying all accrued fees plus the delinquency fee and showing CE compliance; after 5 years it can no longer be renewed at all.
records.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §5070.6 (delinquent renewal / 5-year window) and §5070.5 (permit expiration on birth-month); delinquency-fee formula at §163.5; extra CE at 16 CCR §81

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: No dollar figure is codified anywhere -- C.R.S. 12-20-202 delegates fee-setting to the DORA Director, published only on the online licensing portal, not in statute or rule. There is simply no primary-law dollar figure to cite for this one.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 3 CCR 705-1 Rule 1.9(K)(1): the applicant must complete BOTH the full 80-hour requirement for the CPE period immediately preceding reinstatement, AND 10 hours for each full quarter the certificate was expired in the current period (up to 80 more) -- up to 160 hours total catch-up. These hours can't also count toward CPE owed for the remainder of the period after reinstatement.
records.lapse_trigger: A certificate not renewed by its expiration date enters 'Expired' status (Rule 1.9(J)(1)). A 60-day grace period allows renewal by paying the renewal fee plus a late fee with no penalty; after that, the certificate is fully Expired and the holder cannot hold out as a CPA.
records.citation: 3 CCR 705-1, Rule 1.9(J) (Expired Status) and Rule 1.9(K) (Reinstatement)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Regs. Conn. State Agencies §20-280-25(g) requires paying 'the current year's renewal fee' to reinstate a license lapsed more than 90 days (and up to 3 years) -- the board's own fee schedule sets that fee at $565.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 40 hours of CPE earned in the single year immediately preceding the reinstatement application (rather than spread over the normal cycle).
records.lapse_trigger: Licenses expire annually on December 31; a late application is accepted through January 31. If not received by February 1, the license lapses. Lapsed 90 days or less: reinstate by simple application. Lapsed more than 90 days but less than 3 years: reinstate at the department's discretion on the fee + 40-hour CPE terms above. Lapsed 3+ years: must apply for an entirely new license.
records.citation: Regs. Conn. State Agencies §20-280-25 (Renewal and reinstatement of license and continuing professional education requirement)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Board's own fee page lists Renewal $110, Late Renewal $50, and Reinstatement $295 as distinct line items.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 17 DCMR §2530.3: reinstating a license lapsed less than 5 years requires 40 hours of approved CPE for each year of non-renewal, capped at 120 hours -- this replaces, not stacks on top of, the normal 80-hour/2-year requirement.
records.lapse_trigger: Licenses are on a 2-year cycle expiring December 31 of even-numbered years. Failing to renew by that date lapses the license; DC's general licensing law separately tiers late penalties ($75/$150/$350) by how long a license has been lapsed, though the Board's own posted flat $295 reinstatement fee is the figure actually applied.
records.citation: 17 DCMR §2530.3 (reinstatement CPE); D.C. Code §47-2851.10 (lapsed and reinstated licenses); §47-2853.10 (Board fee-schedule authority)
records.data_gap_note: The $295 reinstatement fee is stated on the Board's own page, but no codified DCMR fee schedule or DC Register notice stating that exact number could be located -- only the general statutory authority for the Board to set fees. Recommend a manual check with the Board if you want the fee confirmed against a published rule rather than just the agency's own page.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: No fixed dollar figure is published. 24 Del. C. §124 requires the regular renewal fee plus an additional late/reinstatement processing fee (the Board's own fee page says the late fee equals 50% of the renewal fee) -- but the renewal fee itself isn't published as a fixed number ('you are notified of the amount at the time of renewal'), so no flat total can be honestly stated.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: No extra CPE beyond the standard requirement: 24 Del. C. §124 requires only proof the standing 80-hour biennial requirement (24 Del. Admin. Code §100-7.2.1) has been met, not an additional amount.
records.lapse_trigger: Permits expire June 30 of odd-numbered years. A lapsed permit may be reinstated within 1 year of the lapse, at the Board's discretion; if not reinstated within that window, the permit terminates and the holder must reapply as a brand-new applicant.
records.citation: 24 Del. C. §124 (Renewals); §108 (expiration/renewal cycle); 24 Del. Admin. Code §100-7.2 (CPE requirements)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Reinstatement-of-a-null-and-void-license application fee (Fla. Admin. Code r. 61H1-31.015). Reinstatement from null-and-void is discretionary (board must find good-faith effort defeated by illness/hardship, s. 473.313(5), Fla. Stat.) -- not a routine online renewal. A separate $25 delinquent-status fee may also apply but could not be independently confirmed against a codified rule.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: Two-step climb of 120 hours each (Fla. Admin. Code r. 61H1-33.006): 120 hrs to move null-and-void back to delinquent, then another 120 hrs to move delinquent back to active. 160 hours above Florida's normal 80-hour biennial requirement; all must fall within the 24 months preceding the application.
records.lapse_trigger: License goes DELINQUENT on January 1 following failure to report CPE for biennial renewal; if not cured, remains delinquent for 2 years and then AUTOMATICALLY becomes NULL AND VOID (Fla. Admin. Code r. 61H1-30.030), no further board action required.
records.citation: Fla. Admin. Code r. 61H1-31.015 ($250 reinstatement fee); r. 61H1-30.030 (2-year automatic null-and-void trigger); r. 61H1-33.006 (120+120-hr CPE, 8 ethics hrs/step); s. 473.313(5), Fla. Stat. (discretionary reinstatement)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Non-refundable reinstatement fee (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. r. 20-10-.04(1)(a)), payable in addition to completing the CPE catch-up requirement.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 40 hours of CPE for each year since the license last renewed, capped at 160 hours (double the normal 80-hour/2-year renewal). At least 20% of the total must be in accounting/auditing subjects, and at least 80 hours must fall within the 2 years immediately preceding the application; no carryover allowed.
records.lapse_trigger: Licenses expire December 31 of odd-numbered years. A 4-month penalty period follows, during which the license can still be renewed by paying a $100 penalty fee plus the renewal fee. After that window closes, reinstatement (not renewal) is required.
records.citation: Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. r. 20-10-.04 (Reinstatement); r. 20-10-.02 (Biennial Renewal); r. 20-10-.03 (Penalty Period/Late Renewal)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Board's own fee page: $204 to restore a lapsed individual license, vs. $152 for on-time renewal. Firm permit-to-practice restoration is separate and higher ($360 entity / $128 sole proprietor).
records.penalty_cpe_notes: HAR §16-71-35 requires making up any CPE deficiency from the standard 80-hour biennial requirement before the Board approves the permit to practice -- completion of an existing shortfall, not an additional penalty on top of the normal requirement.
records.lapse_trigger: Licenses and permits renew biennially by December 31 of odd-numbered years. Per the Board's own page, licenses not renewed by the expiration date are unlicensed and may not practice.
records.citation: Hawaii Administrative Rules Title 16, Chapter 71, §16-71-2 (biennial renewal) and §16-71-35 (deficiency and carryover hours)
records.data_gap_note: The $204/$360/$128 fee figures are confirmed only on the Board's own page -- HAR Chapter 71 defers the actual renewal/restoration fee amounts to a separate fee-schedule chapter (16-53) that could not be located at a working URL. Treat the dollar figures as board-confirmed but not yet codified-rule-confirmed until that chapter is located and cited directly.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: IDAPA 24.30.01.400 sets the reinstatement fee as the sum of unpaid license fees for the preceding 3 cycles -- $360 is the representative case (3 x $120 active annual fee), varying with how many cycles were missed. Idaho Code §54-212(6) caps the total at $500.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: IDAPA 24.30.01.117: 80 hours of CPE completed within the 12 months immediately before applying for reinstatement -- the same 80-hour total as normal renewal, just compressed from a 2-year cycle into a single 12-month lookback window.
records.lapse_trigger: Licenses expire June 30 each year. Renewing after July 1 but before August 1 only requires a $100 late fee; if still unrenewed by August 1, the license is deemed lapsed and subject to reinstatement, and the holder may not use the CPA title or perform reserved services.
records.citation: IDAPA 24.30.01.117 (Reinstatement and Re-entry); 24.30.01.108 (Annual Renewal and Late Fee); 24.30.01.400 (Fees) -- current post-2023-renumbering

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Statutory cap, not a flat fee: $50 restoration fee plus all lapsed annual renewal fees ($40/yr Licensed CPA, $30/yr Registered CPA), capped so the total 'shall not exceed $260' (68 Ill. Admin. Code 1420.40). Restoring from voluntary inactive status costs only the current renewal fee instead.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: No extra CPE beyond the normal 120-hour/3-year total (68 Ill. Admin. Code 1420.60/1420.70) -- restoration just requires those 120 hours to fall within the 3 years immediately preceding the restoration application, not an additional amount.
records.lapse_trigger: Individual license expires September 30 every 3 years (firm license: November 30) if not renewed in the 2-month pre-expiration window. No grace period -- practicing on an expired license is unlicensed activity from the day after expiration (68 Ill. Admin. Code 1420.80).
records.citation: 68 Ill. Admin. Code 1420.60 (Restoration); 1420.40 (Fees); 1420.80 (Renewals)
records.data_gap_note: No separate penalty CPE/ethics hour figures are published because the rule imposes the same standard 120-hr/4-ethics-hr load already required at ordinary renewal, just with a tighter lookback window -- not an additional number. IDFPR's own site does not publish CPA-specific restoration dollar figures on a single page (its general reactivation-fee table explicitly excludes CPAs); the board-page leg of the 2-source rule is satisfied by the Public Accounting landing page instead, with the exact fee formula confirmed only in the codified rule text.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: $155 if the license has been lapsed 3 years or less; $190 (the current initial application fee) if lapsed more than 3 years, per 872 IAC 1-3-14 and IC 25-1-8-6.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 120 total CPE hours completed no earlier than 3 years before the reinstatement application, at least 10% in accounting/auditing, no more than 50% via self-study -- these hours can't double-count toward the licensee's ongoing 3-year renewal cycle.
records.lapse_trigger: Certificates run on a 3-year cycle. A certificate becomes lapsed/expired when the holder fails to renew (application, fee, and CPE) by the cycle's expiration date. 872 IAC 1-3-14 splits the reinstatement path by lapse length: 60 days or less is a lighter path; more than 60 days requires the full reinstatement application; more than 3 years triggers a heavier track (fee = current initial application fee, plus board-ordered remediation).
records.citation: 872 IAC 1-3-14 (Reinstatement of Lapsed Certificate); fee tiers at IC 25-1-8-6(d)(5); CPE/ethics table at 872 IAC 1-3-16

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Formula, capped at $1,000: a $100 base reinstatement fee + the current annual renewal fee ($100 active/$50 inactive) + $25 for each month the license was lapsed (waived if the licensee didn't practice or hold out as a CPA during the lapse).
records.penalty_cpe_notes: No CPE added purely as a penalty -- reinstating to active status requires the standard 120 hours of CPE (the normal 3-year-cycle total, including the required ethics hours) earned in the 3 years immediately preceding the application. Reinstating to inactive status requires no CPE.
records.lapse_trigger: Certificates/licenses expire annually on June 30, with a 30-day grace period (through July 30) to renew by paying a late-renewal penalty. If still unrenewed after that 30-day window, the certificate lapses automatically -- no separate notice or board action is required.
records.citation: Iowa Admin. Code r. 481-1032.1/1032.2 (fee schedule + reinstatement formula; formerly 193A-12.1/12.2); r. 481-1025.3/1025.4 (renewal deadline, grace period, lapse trigger; formerly 193A-5.3/5.4); r. 481-1030.5(7) (CPE to reinstate to active status; formerly 193A-10.5(7))
records.verification_history: 2026-08-14: citations renumbered -- All Iowa Admin. Code 193A accountancy chapters were editorially transferred to Inspections and Appeals [481] chapters 1021-1040 by IAC Supplement 2026-06-10 (2023 Iowa Acts SF 514); the old 193A chapter PDFs are now transfer-notice stubs. Chapter 1032 (FEES) fetched in full: 1032.2(1) confirms the recorded formula verbatim ($100 + renewal fee + $25/month of expired registration, capped at $1,000) and 1032.2(3) confirms the monthly-penalty waiver for licensees who did not practice during the lapse.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: K.A.R. 74-12-1(e): $247.50 if more than one year remains in the current biennial period at application time, or $123.75 if one year or less remains.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 40 hours of qualifying CE completed within the 12 months preceding the reinstatement application (K.S.A. 1-310(g)) -- half the normal 80-hour/2-year total, but concentrated into one year. These hours cannot also be counted toward the next renewal (K.A.R. 74-4-10).
records.lapse_trigger: Permit expires biennially on the next July 1 after issuance/renewal. Late renewal is possible within 12 months of expiration; beyond 12 months, formal reinstatement (not simple late renewal) is required.
records.citation: K.S.A. 1-310(g) (reinstatement trigger, 40-hour CPE requirement); K.A.R. 74-12-1(e) (fee schedule); K.A.R. 74-4-10 (2-hour ethics component)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Flat $200 reinstatement fee (201 KAR 1:140 Section 3(1)(c)) -- separate from a $100 late fee that applies if renewal is completed within the Aug 1-Sep 1 grace window before the license fully expires.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: No extra CPE beyond normal renewal -- reinstatement requires documenting the same total (60 or 80 hours, whichever applied when the license expired) owed for a normal renewal, completed within the 2 years before the reinstatement application.
records.lapse_trigger: Licenses renew biennially (odd-numbered licenses in odd years, even in even years) with a July 1-31 renewal window; an Aug 1-Sep 1 grace period allows renewal with a $100 late fee. A license not renewed by September 1 expires. Reinstatement applies once a license has been expired more than 1 month or voluntarily surrendered.
records.citation: 201 KAR 1:140, Section 3 (Procedures for reinstatement or reissuance of a CPA license)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: No single flat fee -- three different mechanisms exist depending on how long the certificate has been lapsed. LAC 46:XIX Sec1105.B sets a same-year reinstatement fee equal to twice the current renewal fee (~$240); La. R.S. 37:74.1 separately caps a formal reinstatement-application fee at $500 for a fully expired/inactive certificate; the board's own fee table also shows an escalating monthly delinquent-fee schedule ($200-$700). The board's page itself says 'Reinstatement applications -- (contact the office)' rather than publishing one number.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 120 total CPE hours (not additive on top of the normal 80) completed within the 3 years preceding the reinstatement application, per LAC 46:XIX Sec1105.D -- confirmed on both the codified rule and the board's own page.
records.lapse_trigger: A certificate expires December 31 each year if not renewed. Missing renewal before February 1 adds a delinquent fee equal to the current renewal fee; missing it before March 1 makes the certificate expired/lapsed and doubles the reinstatement renewal fee.
records.citation: La. Admin. Code tit. 46, Pt. XIX, Sec1105.B & Sec1105.D; see also La. R.S. 37:76(B) and La. R.S. 37:74.1
records.data_gap_note: The reinstatement fee is genuinely unresolved: three different dollar figures/mechanisms exist across the board's own materials (twice the renewal fee, a $500 statutory cap, and a separate monthly delinquent schedule) and none reconciles cleanly with the others, so no single dollar figure is published here rather than picking one. The 3-hour ethics figure is currently sourced only from the board's own page, not independently confirmed in the codified rule text (checked Sec1301, Sec1303, Sec1319 -- none states an hour figure). Recommend a manual check with the board before citing a specific reinstatement dollar amount.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Reinstatement applications are charged the standard $35/yr CPA license fee (02-041 C.M.R. ch.10 Sec5(1)) -- Maine has no separate reinstatement-specific fee line item. A late-renewal cure within 90 days of expiration instead draws a separate $50 uniform late fee (02-041 C.M.R. ch.11 Sec2(1)).
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 02-280 C.M.R. ch.5 Sec7: 80 hours of CPE completed in the 24 months immediately preceding the reinstatement application -- the same standard 40-hr/year rate as ordinary renewal (ch.5 Sec8A), not extra volume.
records.lapse_trigger: Licenses expire annually. A license may be renewed online up to 90 days after expiration by paying the fee plus the $50 late fee. If not renewed within 90 days, the Board may (within 2 years of the original expiration) waive new-applicant requirements and instead allow reinstatement via the 80-hour CPE path above; beyond 2 years, the former licensee must requalify as a brand-new applicant.
records.citation: 02-280 C.M.R. ch. 5, Sections 6-7 (License Expiration, Renewal, and Reinstatement); 32 M.R.S. Sec12234(1)-(2); fees at 02-041 C.M.R. ch. 10, Sec5(1) and ch. 11, Sec2(1)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Double the standard $63 renewal fee (COMAR 09.24.01.09.B(9)/(4)). Charged as soon as the license's 2-year expiration date passes; the Board's FAQ states it currently cannot be waived.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: Same standard 80-hour/2-year total as ordinary renewal, not an extra amount -- the catch is timing: those 80 hours must be earned within 2 years of the reinstatement application date (COMAR 09.24.02.05.A) and can't also be counted toward the next renewal cycle.
records.lapse_trigger: Not renewed by the license's fixed 2-year expiration date. No statutory outer time limit was found after which reinstatement becomes unavailable.
records.citation: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 2-314 (Reinstatement); COMAR 09.24.01.09.B (fees); COMAR 09.24.02.03 (80-hr/4-ethics-hr CE requirement); COMAR 09.24.02.05.A (2-year CE lookback)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: No single flat fee. Reinstatement requires all back renewal fees for each missed 2-year cycle, plus a late fee (the general Division of Registration late fee is $57), plus the current $161 renewal fee -- a computed total, not a published flat figure.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: Applies only once a license 'has not been renewed for at least two renewal periods' (roughly a 4+ year lapse): 160 hours of CPE within the 24 months before reissue, at least 80 of which must be in the attest function (M.G.L. c. 112 Sec87B(c)) -- double the normal 80-hour/2-year requirement. A shorter lapse (one cycle or less) requires only the normal CPE already due, no extra hours.
records.lapse_trigger: A license is issued/renewed for a 2-year term expiring the last day of June of the following year. Missing that date lapses the license; 252 CMR 2.16 splits treatment by whether it's lapsed one renewal cycle or less vs. more than one cycle (the latter triggering the enhanced 160-hour CPE requirement above).
records.citation: M.G.L. c. 112, Sec87B(a) and (c); 252 CMR 2.16 (Reinstatement of Lapsed/Expired License); 252 CMR 2.14 (Mandatory CPE)
records.data_gap_note: The board's own mass.gov page blocks automated access site-wide, so this fact could not be freshly re-confirmed by an automated check at publish time -- corroborated instead by two independent primary-law sources (the codified regulation, 252 CMR 2.14/2.16, and the enabling statute, M.G.L. c. 112 Sec87B, both fetched directly). Recommend a manual check of the board's page if you want to see it firsthand.
records.verification_history: 2026-08-03: source_url repointed -- mass.gov/orgs/board-of-registration-in-public-accountancy went dead; the board's page moved to boards.mass.gov, confirmed live.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: $100 application-processing fee (MCL 338.2211) applies to a relicensure application under R 338.5230 (that rule requires 'the required fee' without stating an amount itself). A separate $20 late-renewal fee applies only within the 60-day cure window before true lapse.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: Mich. Admin. Code R 338.5230: 40 hours of CE completed within the 12 months immediately preceding the relicensure filing (1 additional year allowed to cure a deficiency) -- the same ~40/yr annualized rate as normal renewal, just compressed in timing. Licenses lapsed 3+ years additionally require proof of a valid unrevoked CPA certificate and may require passing all or part of the exam.
records.lapse_trigger: A license lapses automatically the day after its biennial July 31 expiration date if not renewed (MCL 339.411(1)) -- no separate notice required. A 60-day grace window allows curing by paying the normal fee plus a $20 late fee; beyond that, relicensure (with the CE catch-up above) is required.
records.citation: Mich. Admin. Code R 338.5230 (Relicensure; continuing education); MCL 339.411 (lapse/relicensure trigger); MCL 338.2211 and 338.2206 (fee amounts)
records.data_gap_note: The board's own michigan.gov page blocks automated access site-wide, so this fact could not be freshly re-confirmed by an automated check at publish time -- the codified rule and statute (R 338.5230, MCL 339.411, 338.2206, 338.2211) were fetched directly and state these figures; the $100 fee is inferred with high but not full confidence as the correct line item, since no board document explicitly labeled 'reinstatement fee' could be reached. Recommend a manual check of the board's page if you want it confirmed firsthand.
records.verification_history: 2026-08-03: source_url repointed -- the old .../prof/accountants path 404s; .../prof/accountancy is the correct current LARA Board of Accountancy page, confirmed live in a real browser.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Flat statutory fee: 'applications for reinstatement, $20' (Minn. Stat. Sec326A.04, subd. 5(b)(9)) -- distinct from a separate $50 annual late-processing fee for renewals filed late but before expiration.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: Not a fixed number -- Minn. Stat. Sec326A.09 gives the board discretion to require up to 120 hours of CPE representing what would have been earned had the credential been held continuously during the lapse (capped at one full 3-year cycle), plus any other conditions the board finds appropriate.
records.lapse_trigger: Certificates must be renewed annually, expiring December 31. If not renewed, or if suspended, revoked, or surrendered, the credential becomes expired/invalid and the former holder must petition the board for reinstatement before practicing again.
records.citation: Minn. Stat. Sec326A.09 (Reinstatement); Sec326A.04, subd. 2 and subd. 5(b) (issuance/renewal timing and fees); Minn. R. 1105.2560 (Renewal of Certificates)
records.data_gap_note: The $20 fee is confirmed directly in codified statute, but the board's own renewal pages could not be independently confirmed to state the figure in plain language -- repeated attempts hit a bot-verification challenge rather than page content. Recommend a manual check of the board's page if you want it confirmed firsthand.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: $310 = $200 Board Processing Fee for Reinstatement + $110 Registration Fee for Reinstatement (Board's Schedule of Fees). On top of any delinquent back-fees (capped at 3 years, $110/yr) and a $150 late fee -- total cost varies by how long the license was lapsed.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 40 CPE hours for each 12-month compliance period missed, capped at 120 hours (3 years' worth), earned within 36 months of the reinstatement application (Rule 2.4.4) -- a ceiling, not a fixed add-on. Must include the standard 3-hour ethics and 1-hour MS law/regulations courses within that total, the same triennial requirement normal licensees owe, not an extra requirement.
records.lapse_trigger: A license is automatically cancelled if the holder fails to register and pay the annual fee by January 1 AND then fails to cure within 10 days of a certified-mail default notice. A license can also be lost via revocation, suspension, or voluntary surrender, all triggering the same reinstatement track.
records.citation: Miss. Code Ann. Sec73-33-7(2),(4); 30 Miss. Code R. Part 1, Ch. 2, Rules 2.3 (Registration) and 2.4 (Reinstatement); Schedule of Fees, Appendix to 30 Miss. Code R. Part 1

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Flat $200 'CPA Reinstatement of License Fee' (20 CSR 2010-2.160(1)(G)). A separate $50/month delinquent fee applies for failure to timely renew, and all required fees/penalties for any period practicing without a current license must also be paid -- total cost can exceed $200.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 20 CSR 2010-2.075(1)(A): 40 hours of CPE completed in the 12 months immediately preceding the reinstatement application -- the same 40-hour annual amount already required of an active licensee, not a stacked extra.
records.lapse_trigger: Licenses run a 2-year period, October 1 to September 30. If not renewed by September 30, the license is expired but can still be late-renewed through December 31 of that year. If no renewal is filed by December 31, the license becomes 'lapsed,' and the holder may not practice or use the CPA title.
records.citation: 20 CSR 2010-2.075 (Reinstatement -- CPE requirement); 20 CSR 2010-2.160(1)(G),(L)2 (fees); 20 CSR 2010-4.035 (Inactive, Expired, and Lapsed Licenses)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: No codified dollar figure exists. The Board's own License Reactivation page says to submit 'the appropriate fee' without stating an amount; the closest confirmed figure is the general late-renewal penalty of 100% of the renewal fee (on a $125 active renewal fee, roughly $250 total), which is a late-fee formula, not a confirmed flat reinstatement fee.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: No extra CPE beyond the standard requirement -- reinstatement (ARM 24.201.2161) requires only the standard 120-hour/3-year CPE requirement (including its 2-hour ethics subset) already used for ordinary renewal, not an added penalty.
records.lapse_trigger: Permits and firm registrations must be renewed annually by December 31; missing that date adds a 100% late fee and, per general licensing rules, lapses the license. Returning to active status requires filing a License Reactivation Application and documenting the standard CPE requirement for the 3 years preceding the application.
records.citation: Mont. Admin. R. 24.201.2161 (Reinstatement), incorporating 24.201.2106 (CPE Requirement); 24.101.413 (Renewal Dates and Requirements); 24.101.403 (Fees)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Board's own reinstatement application form states a flat $200 fee. Neb. Rev. Stat. Sec1-136(3) authorizes the board to set this fee for a permit reissued after failure to renew within 3 years, capped at $300 -- $200 is within, but not itself stated by, the codified cap.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 288 Neb. Admin. Code ch. 8, Sec010: 120 hours of approved CPE completed within the 3 calendar years immediately preceding the reinstatement application -- these hours cannot also count toward the next renewal cycle. Notably this figure IS stated explicitly in the codified rule (unlike Nebraska's ordinary-renewal CPE requirement, which this site's separate CPE-hours dataset found is never stated as a number in codified law, only in board guidance).
records.lapse_trigger: Nebraska's mechanism centers on 'inactive' status rather than a distinct 'lapsed' label: an active permit expires June 30 (annually or biennially by age parity); a CPE compliance failure triggers a certified-mail Notice of Non-Compliance and, after a hearing, the board may decline to renew the permit. A holder who fails to apply for a new permit within 3 years of the last permit's expiration loses the right to reinstatement unless the board finds the failure excusable.
records.citation: 288 Neb. Admin. Code, ch. 8, Sec010 (Reinstatement); Sec009.01-.04 (non-compliance/waiver procedure); Neb. Rev. Stat. Sec1-136(3) (3-year forfeiture rule and fee cap)
records.data_gap_note: The $200 fee is confirmed on the Board's own reinstatement application form (a real board document), but the codified rule only sets a $300 statutory ceiling and delegates the exact amount to the board's own fee schedule, which doesn't appear separately codified. Recommend a manual check with the board if you want the fee confirmed against a published rule rather than just the agency's own form.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: No single flat fee covers the plain 'missed the deadline, renewed late' scenario. A simple late renewal (before lapsing further) costs a $150 late fee (capped at $200 by NAC 628.016(3)(d)) on top of the $175 standard annual fee. A separate $250 fee (NAC 628.016/628.110(4)) applies specifically to reinstatement from retired/inactive status, not ordinary late renewal.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: Branches by how far the lapse progressed: reinstatement from retired/inactive status requires 40 CPE hours (incl. 4 ethics) in the preceding 12 months (NAC 628.110(4)); reinstatement after voluntary surrender requires 40 hours plus back fees (NAC 628.110(5)); reinstatement after revocation or disciplinary surrender requires 80 hours (incl. 8 ethics) in the preceding 12 months (NAC 628.110(6)).
records.lapse_trigger: Permits expire automatically every December 31. Renewal (with the $175 fee) is due by January 31 of the following year; after that a $150 late fee applies and the holder may not practice until delinquent fees/penalties are paid. Failing to obtain the annual permit within 60 days after the prior permit's expiration is a ground for the board to revoke the certificate, unless excused.
records.data_gap_note: Nevada does not codify a single flat fee or CPE figure that applies uniformly to every lapsed scenario -- the applicable fee/hours depend on which status track applies (late renewal vs. retired/inactive reinstatement vs. revocation), and whether/when a simple missed deadline converts into a formal revocation is discretionary, not on an automatic timeline. Both the board's own page and the codified NRS/NAC text were checked and are internally consistent, but neither states one unambiguous number for the general case, hence the null fields above rather than picking one branch's figure to represent all cases. The board's current renewal page confirms the $175 annual renewal fee and $150 late fee this record cites.
records.verification_history: 2026-08-13: the board's old nvaccountancy.com domain now silently redirects to a relaunched site -- source_url repointed to the live renewal page there, which still confirms the $175 annual fee and $150 late fee (CITE-19 sweep).

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: $201 per N.H. Code Admin. R. Plc 1002.01, Table 1002.1 -- the SAME figure as a normal on-time renewal fee; the rule does not impose a separate, higher fee for reinstating a license lapsed 1 year or less. If lapsed more than 1 year, the licensee must reapply as a brand-new initial applicant (same $201 fee, but the full initial-licensure process).
records.penalty_cpe_notes: No extra or prorated catch-up CPE hours are required to reinstate a license lapsed 1 year or less for non-renewal (Ac 401.08) -- only the standard renewal application package and a work-history resume covering the lapse period. (A different, separate path -- returning to active practice from voluntary inactive status -- does require 80 hours of CPE including 4 ethics hours regardless of duration; that is not the same as reinstating a lapsed license.)
records.lapse_trigger: A certificate expires 2 years from the day it was issued. If not renewed by that date, it becomes 'Lapsed for Non-Renewal.' Reinstatement (Ac 401.08) is available only for licenses lapsed no more than 1 year; beyond that, the holder must reapply as a brand-new initial applicant.
records.citation: N.H. Code Admin. R. Ac 401.08 (Reinstatement of a License Lapsed for Non-Renewal); Ac 401.01, 401.03, 403.01; fee at Plc 1002.01, Table 1002.1
records.data_gap_note: The board's own oplc.nh.gov page blocks automated access, so this fact could not be freshly re-confirmed by an automated check at publish time -- content was instead confirmed directly against New Hampshire's official codified Code of Administrative Rules (gc.nh.gov), reading the actual current rule and fee-table text. Recommend a manual check of the board's page if you want it confirmed firsthand.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Flat $150 reinstatement fee (N.J.A.C. 13:29-1.5), plus the current triennial renewal fee ($135), the past-due renewal fee for the prior triennial period, and (if within the 30-day grace window) a separate $50 late fee.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: No extra CPE beyond normal -- reinstatement requires evidence of completing the standard 120-credit triennial requirement (min. 20/year) for the lapsed period, per N.J.A.C. 13:29-1.9(a)(6), not an added penalty amount.
records.lapse_trigger: A license runs a 3-year cycle. A 30-day grace period after expiration allows renewal by fee + late fee. If not renewed within 30 days, the license 'shall be suspended without a hearing' (N.J.A.C. 13:29-1.7(e)) -- this suspension-for-non-renewal is New Jersey's functional lapsed status, triggering the reinstatement track.
records.citation: N.J.A.C. 13:29-1.9 (License Reinstatement Procedures); triggered by suspension under 13:29-1.7(e); fee at 13:29-1.5

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Board fee schedule: 'Reinstatement of Cancelled Certificate: $175' -- separate from the $130 annual renewal fee and $100 late-renewal penalty. The codified rule requires payment of the current year's renewal fee plus reinstatement requirements but doesn't itemize the $175 figure itself; the dollar amount is set on the board's own fee schedule.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 16.60.3.15 NMAC: 40 hours of CPE for each year the certificate was expired, not to exceed 200 hours. If expired more than 36 months, at least 120 of those hours must be from the preceding 36 months.
records.lapse_trigger: A certificate lapses or expires from non-renewal when the holder misses their individual renewal deadline (the last day of their birth month). The board's own FAQ states the certificate is canceled if not renewed within 90 days of expiration.
records.citation: 16.60.3.12 NMAC (Reinstatement Requirements); 16.60.3.15 NMAC (CPE Required to Obtain or Maintain an Active License)
records.data_gap_note: The $175 fee and the '90 days to cancellation' trigger are confirmed only on the board's own pages, not independently in the codified NMAC text reachable this pass (the rule authorizes fees without stating the dollar amount, and doesn't state the 90-day figure in the sections checked). The 40-hour/year (max 200) penalty CPE figure IS directly confirmed in the codified rule. Recommend a manual check with the board for the fee/90-day figures.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: No flat fee -- a lapsed/reactivating CPA owes the normal triennial re-registration fee ($292 total: $242 registration incl. surcharge + $50 CE processing fee) PLUS a $10 late-filing fee for each month registration was delayed (N.Y. Educ. Law Sec6502(3)).
records.penalty_cpe_notes: To reactivate from inactive or not-registered status, at least 24 hours of acceptable CPE completed in the 12 months immediately before filing to reactivate (8 NYCRR Sec70.9(b)(6)); more may be required if the licensee was practicing while lapsed.
records.lapse_trigger: Registration becomes 'Not registered' when a licensee doesn't file a triennial renewal application/fee by the start of the next registration period. A licensee resuming practice after a lapse may not practice without actual possession of a current registration certificate; a $10/month late fee attaches to any delayed registration.
records.citation: N.Y. Educ. Law Sec6502(3) (late-filing fee / lapse of registration); 8 NYCRR Sec70.9(b)(6) (24-hour CPE to reactivate); base fee set by Educ. Law Sec7404

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Reissuance-of-forfeited-certificate application fee (21 NCAC 08J .0106(b)(1)), 'plus penalties' per the Board's own fee schedule -- no primary-law source ties a specific extra dollar figure to routine late-renewal forfeiture, so treat as a floor, not a hard ceiling.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 40 CPE hours completed in the 12 months immediately preceding the reinstatement application (21 NCAC 08J .0106(b)(3)) -- the same total as one year's ordinary renewal, not extra hours. NC does not require make-up CPE for years spent forfeited.
records.lapse_trigger: License is FORFEITED if not renewed by July 1, the Board mails a demand letter, and renewal (application + CPE + fee) still isn't completed within 30 days of that letter's mailing date.
records.citation: 21 NCAC 08J .0106 (Forfeiture of Certificate and Reissuance), with 21 NCAC 08J .0101/.0105(c), 21 NCAC 08F .0504, and N.C. Gen. Stat. § 93-12(15)/(7a)/(9)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: N.D. Admin. Code Sec3-02-02-08 caps the reinstatement fee at $200 (payable in addition to the applicable annual renewal fee) -- $200 reported here is the rule's ceiling, not a separately published lower flat figure.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: No reinstatement-specific extra CPE hours found -- the rule requires only that the applicant satisfy the standard, ongoing 120-hour/3-year requirement (with 6 ethics hours) already in force, not an added penalty tier.
records.lapse_trigger: Failing to pay the annual renewal fee by June 30 draws a late fee (up to $100); if still unpaid by July 31, the certificate/license 'is deemed involuntarily relinquished and not renewed' effective August 1, triggering the reinstatement requirements and fee.
records.citation: N.D. Admin. Code Sec3-02-02-04 (annual renewal fees / lapse-relinquishment trigger) and Sec3-02-02-08 (reinstatement fees)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: No flat fee -- a monthly late-filing charge under ORC 4701.10(D)-(E): up to $100/month (cap $1,200) for a practicing permit holder, up to $50/month (cap $300) for a registration/non-practicing holder. If the Board finds 'excusable neglect' (ORC 4701.10(F)), it may instead set a reduced fee (not exceeding $50 plus the standard triennial permit fee per lapsed period).
records.penalty_cpe_notes: Same 120-credit/3-year total as ordinary renewal (Ohio Admin. Code 4701-15-02(A)), but reinstatement (OAC 4701-15-09) requires all 120 within the 36 months immediately preceding the application AND subject-matter minimums ordinary renewal doesn't impose: at least 24 credits in accounting/auditing/assurance/attestation, at least 24 in taxation.
records.lapse_trigger: Permits/registrations expire December 31 on a staggered triennial cohort cycle (not one date for all licensees). Failing to renew within ONE YEAR of that expiration date suspends the underlying CPA certificate/PA registration (ORC 4701.10(F)) until accrued late fees are paid or a reduced fee is approved.
records.citation: Ohio Rev. Code § 4701.10(A),(B),(D),(E),(F); Ohio Admin. Code 4701-15-02(D), 4701-15-09 (120 credits/36 months, 24 A&A, 24 tax, 3 ethics)
records.data_gap_note: No flat reinstatement fee is published because Ohio's own law sets a formula/cap, not a flat number, stated in plain terms above instead. The Board's own fees page is live and was read directly, including its "Late and Back Fees" tab: "Late fees for expired licenses accrue at a rate of $50/month (to a maximum amount of $300) for Registrations and Permits, and $100/month (to a maximum amount of $1,200) for Permit - Employed in Public Accounting" -- matches this record's figures exactly.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Flat $125 fee applies only if reinstatement is sought within the first year after revocation/cancellation (OAC 10:15-27-10). If more than 1 year has passed, the fee instead equals the accumulated registration/permit fees for the lapse period, capped at $5,000 by 59 O.S. Sec15.14.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: Formula: 40 CPE hours for each calendar year an exemption was claimed or CPE went unreported, capped at 120 hours total (OAC 10:15-30-9) -- catch-up to the normal 120-hour/3-year requirement, not hours in excess of it.
records.lapse_trigger: An individual license must renew by the last day of the holder's birth month; it is considered lapsed the day after that deadline. It is then automatically revoked if fees remain unpaid within 30 calendar days after expiration. A certificate revoked 5+ years may not be renewed or reinstated at all.
records.citation: OAC 10:15-27-10 (Reinstatement fee); 59 O.S. Sec15.14 (Expiration and Renewal, automatic-revocation trigger and fee ceilings); OAC 10:15-23-1 (lapse trigger)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Formula: a $225 non-refundable reinstatement application fee (OAR 801-010-0010) plus the standard $255 active biennial renewal fee for each lapsed renewal period -- total scales with how long the license was lapsed.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: OAR 801-010-0130: normal CPE hours for the lookback window PLUS a flat 16-hour penalty on top -- 96 total hours if lapsed less than 2 years, 176 total if lapsed 2-6 years, all within the 12 months before applying. Lapsed more than 6 years, reinstatement by CPE is unavailable.
records.lapse_trigger: A license not renewed by the June 30 biennial deadline enters late-renewal status; if still not renewed within 60 days after the close of that permit period, it automatically lapses and can only be reinstated via a separate application, not renewed directly.
records.citation: OAR 801-010-0130 (Reinstatement Requirements); OAR 801-010-0110 (Renewal); OAR 801-010-0010 (Fees)
records.data_gap_note: The $225/$255 fee figures and the 16-hour CPE penalty are confirmed in the codified rule (OAR 801-010), but the Board's own License-Renewal-Information page describes the lapse/reinstatement mechanics without restating these dollar/hour figures itself. Recommend a manual check of the board's page if you want the numbers confirmed firsthand.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Reinstatement-of-inactive-or-expired-license fee, paid IN ADDITION TO the current $100 biennial renewal fee -- $135 total plus any CPE course costs.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: Same standard 80-hour total as ordinary biennial renewal (49 Pa. Code § 11.62(c)), not an extra amount -- the only difference is the 80 hours must fall within the 24 months immediately preceding the reactivation filing, rather than the fixed biennial period.
records.lapse_trigger: Not renewed by 11:59pm December 31 of odd-numbered years. The Board states explicitly there is no grace period; the license lapses effective January 1 and a reactivation application (not a standard renewal) is required.
records.citation: 49 Pa. Code § 11.4 (fees, $35 reinstatement); § 11.62(c) (reactivation CPE, 80 hrs/24-month lookback); § 11.63(a)(7) (4-hour ethics minimum)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: $500 reinstatement fee plus the $375 triennial renewal fee -- $875 total out-of-pocket (400-RICR-00-00-1.3(B)(1) and 1.13).
records.penalty_cpe_notes: For a license expired under 5 years: the same 120 CPE hours (over the preceding 3 years) as an ordinary renewal -- no extra hours added. If expired 5+ years, an additional 120 hours (240 total) OR a Board-approved CPA exam review course is required instead.
records.lapse_trigger: Rhode Island licenses run a 3-year cycle with an online renewal deadline; missing it immediately drops the license to expired status (Rhode Island recognizes only Active/Expired/Retired, no separate inactive/grace tier), triggering the reinstatement process.
records.citation: 400-RICR-00-00-1.3(B)(1)-(2) (Reinstatement) and 1.3(C)(1) (License status); fee at 400-RICR-00-00-1.13
records.data_gap_note: The board's own renewal/reinstatement page confirms the lockout mechanic and cycle deadline but does not itself restate the $500 fee or CPE-hour figures -- those come from the codified rule alone. Recommend a manual check of the board's page if you want the numbers confirmed firsthand.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Codified reinstatement fee is $500 (S.C. Code Ann. § 40-2-250(F)), paid in addition to the standard $95 annual renewal fee the board lists on its FAQ -- $595 total out-of-pocket.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 40 CPE hours for EACH year the license was lapsed (cumulative catch-up). If lapsed 3+ years, the requirement jumps to 120 hours (completed within the preceding 3 years) plus 6 months of additional qualifying experience.
records.lapse_trigger: Not renewed by February 1; considered lapsed if not renewed by February 15 at 11:59pm.
records.citation: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-2-250 (Renewal of licenses; reinstatement of lapsed licenses), subsections (E)-(G); definitions in § 40-2-20

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Formula: a $100 base renewal fee plus a $100 late fee for each year the certificate was expired (ARSD 20:75:03:03) -- minimum $200 for a lapse under 1 year, escalating by roughly $100/additional year.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: ARSD 20:75:04:08: if lapsed more than 12 months, at least 24 hours of CPE in the preceding 12 months. If lapsed 12 months or less, only the normal CPE the applicant would have owed anyway is required -- catch-up, not a penalty add-on.
records.lapse_trigger: A certificate becomes expired if renewal (application by August 1, with CPE compliance proof) isn't completed by that deadline. A licensee who neither renews, notifies the board, nor surrenders the certificate is deemed to have an expired certificate and may not perform accounting services.
records.citation: ARSD 20:75:03:02 (Non-renewal); 20:75:03:03 (Renewal fees); 20:75:04:08 (Returning active certificate holders)
records.data_gap_note: The board's own FAQ page only generically warns about consequences of lapsing without stating South Dakota's specific dollar/hour figures -- those come from the codified ARSD rule text alone. Recommend a manual check with the board if you want the numbers confirmed firsthand.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Board's reinstatement page states a $250 application fee for reinstatement of an expired individual or firm license.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 80 hours in technical fields of study, all earned within the 6 months immediately preceding the reinstatement application -- explicitly labeled 'penalty hours' that cannot be applied toward subsequent renewal CPE.
records.lapse_trigger: A license is 'delinquent' from 1 day to 6 months past its biennial expiration date ($100 late fee applies). Once more than 6 months past expiration, the license is deemed expired, triggering the reinstatement process above.
records.citation: Tenn. Comp. R. & Regs. 0020-01-.08(6)-(7) (delinquent vs. expired, late fee); 0020-05-.03(6) (80-hour penalty CPE incl. 2 ethics hours)
records.data_gap_note: The $250 reinstatement application fee is stated clearly on the Board's own page, but couldn't be located verbatim in any codified rule reachable this pass (only the separate $100 delinquent/late-renewal fee is codified) -- it may be set by a fee schedule outside the CE/licensing chapters checked. Recommend a manual check with the board if you want the fee confirmed against a published rule.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: No flat fee -- a tiered multiplier of the base renewal fee under 22 TAC § 515.5: 1.5x if expired ≤ 90 days, 2x if expired 90 days–1 year, 3x if expired 1–2 years; at 2+ years (revocation-eligible) the licensee owes all accrued renewal + late fees for the lapsed period, not a simple multiple. At the current $118/yr base individual fee this computes to roughly $177 / $236 / $354 for the first three tiers.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: 22 TAC § 523.112 requires a former licensee reinstating after revocation to 'report the minimum CPE credits missed' rather than a fixed extra/penalty hour count -- no flat figure exists in the rule text.
records.lapse_trigger: Individual licenses renew annually by the last day of the licensee's birth month. Missing that deadline triggers the escalating late-fee tiers above. Failure to complete renewal for 3 consecutive years lets the Board revoke the license under Tex. Occ. Code § 901.502(4); reinstatement after revocation requires Board action, not a simple late renewal.
records.citation: 22 Tex. Admin. Code § 515.5 (Late Filing for Renewal of License); Tex. Occ. Code § 901.502(4); 22 Tex. Admin. Code § 523.112 (Required CPE Participation)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: No dollar figure is codified in Utah Admin. Code R156-26a or the general renewal-procedure rules -- Utah DOPL fees are set/published administratively, not stated in the rule text itself.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: R156-26a-307(1)(b): 80 hours of qualified CPE within the 12 months immediately preceding the reinstatement application (incl. at least 16 hours in accounting/auditing), plus passing the AICPA Professional Ethics exam and the Utah CPA Laws and Rules exam. None of these hours may be applied toward the next renewal's CPE -- effectively a full penalty burden. Waivers exist for continuous out-of-state licensure or inadvertent nonpayment within 24 months.
records.lapse_trigger: Licenses run a 2-year cycle ending December 31 of even-numbered years. A license not renewed before that date automatically expires; continued practice after that is a criminal offense under Utah Code.
records.citation: Utah Admin. Code R156-26a-307 (Reinstatement of Licenses); R156-1-308c(5)(c) (automatic expiration); R156-26a-303b(2) (2-year cycle)
records.data_gap_note: The reinstatement fee dollar amount could not be confirmed: it isn't in the codified rule text, and the Board's own site currently blocks automated access, so this fact could not be freshly re-confirmed at publish time. The CPE/ethics-exam requirements above ARE confirmed directly in the codified rule. Recommend a manual check of the board's page if you want the fee confirmed firsthand.
records.verification_history: 2026-08-03: source_url repointed -- dopl.utah.gov/cpa/ went dead; commerce.utah.gov/dopl/accountancy/ is the current DOPL Accountancy board page, confirmed live.

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Tiered under 3 V.S.A. Sec127(d)(1): the normal $255 biennial renewal fee plus a reinstatement penalty of $100 flat (if reinstated within 30 days of expiration) or, if later, the renewal fee increased by $40 for each additional month late, capped at $1,500 -- total ranges roughly $355 to $1,755. The Board may waive/reduce the penalty for exceptional hardship, with an automatic exemption for active-duty military.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: Board Rule 9.1(c): the same standard CPE requirement (normally 80 hours/2 years) completed during the lapsed period -- no extra/incremental penalty hours found anywhere in the rules reviewed.
records.lapse_trigger: Licenses renew on a fixed biennial schedule (July 31 of odd-numbered years). Failing to return the completed renewal application and fee by that date causes automatic expiration, with no additional grace period described in the rules.
records.citation: 3 V.S.A. Sec127(d)(1)-(3) (reinstatement-penalty statute); 26 V.S.A. Sec56(2) (biennial renewal fee); Vermont Board of Public Accountancy Administrative Rules 8.1-8.2, 9.1(c)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Nonrefundable individual reinstatement fee (firm reinstatement is a separate $500 fee).
records.penalty_cpe_notes: Reinstatement requires the standard 120 CPE hours (earned in the 3 calendar years prior to and including the application year) plus a VBOA-approved ethics course -- this mirrors the standard rolling requirement rather than adding extra hours on top of normal renewal.
records.lapse_trigger: Individual licenses must renew by June 30 each year; per the board's own guidance an unrenewed license automatically expires effective July 1, requiring reinstatement rather than simple renewal.
records.citation: 18VAC5-22-20 (Fees) and 18VAC5-22-180 (Issuance, renewal, and reinstatement of licenses)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Flat $480 fee, confirmed on both the board's reinstatement page and the codified fee schedule (WAC 4-30-038) -- separate from/in addition to any outstanding renewal or late fees.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: No extra CPE hours beyond the normal 120-credit/3-year requirement (WAC 4-30-134(5)(a)), just measured over the 36 months immediately preceding the reinstatement application instead of a fixed calendar cycle. The 4-hour Washington ethics course must fall within the 6 months immediately preceding the application (a recency requirement, not a volume increase); these hours can't be reused toward the next renewal.
records.lapse_trigger: A license lapses if the licensee fails to file a complete renewal application (with CPE certification and fees) by June 30 of the renewal year, effective July 1. Once lapsed, the individual may not use the CPA title or exercise related privileges until reinstated.
records.citation: WAC 4-30-094 (Renewals / lapse trigger); WAC 4-30-124 (Reinstatements); WAC 4-30-134(5) (CPE for reinstatement); WAC 4-30-038 (Fees)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: Formula: $85 reinstatement fee + $85 annual renewal fee + $50 late fee ($220 base) plus $75 for each additional month lapsed past July 31, capped at $445 total (W. Va. C.S.R. Sec1-1-18, confirmed on the board's own renewal page).
records.penalty_cpe_notes: The greater of (a) the CPE hours deficient from the last non-compliant year, or (b) 40 hours total, all completed within the prior 2 calendar years.
records.lapse_trigger: Licenses expire annually June 30; a July 1-31 grace period allows late renewal with a $50 late fee. If not renewed by July 31, the licensee is listed as 'Lapsed' and must file a formal reinstatement application rather than a normal renewal. CPE noncompliance in the prior year also routes into the reinstatement process.
records.citation: W. Va. Code R. Sec1-1-7 (Certificate Renewal, subsections 7.4-7.5) and Sec1-1-18 (Fees)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: DSPS's official fee schedule (Renewal Dates and Fees PDF) states $43 renewal fee / $68 with late fee for Reg Type 1 (CPA) -- the $68 figure is the fee this site reports, cross-checked against the $25 late-fee amount codified in Wis. Stat. 440.08(3)(a) ($43 + $25 = $68). Accy 2.501 cross-references this same fee for both 5+-year late renewal and formal reinstatement.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: Formula: renewing/reinstating 5+ years after the renewal date requires at least 120 CPE credits in the preceding 3 years (Accy 2.501(2)(a)), vs. 80 credits/2 years for renewal within 5 years -- plus, if applicable, verification of exam/education completion and evidence of disciplinary compliance.
records.lapse_trigger: The CPA credential's fixed renewal date is December 14 of each odd-numbered year. If not renewed by then, the license becomes delinquent but can still be restored as a late renewal within 5 years by paying the fee above; beyond 5 years, the enhanced 120-credit/3-year showing and formal reinstatement track apply.
records.citation: Wis. Admin. Code Accy 2.501 (Renewal and reinstatement of individual licenses); Wis. Stat. 440.08(2)-(3) (renewal dates, late fee)

records.reinstatement_fee_notes: 'Activate From Expired Status' fee (061-1 Wyo. Code R. Sec1-13), confirmed on both the board's reactivate-certificate page and the codified fee schedule. A separate, much higher $1,000 'Reinstate' fee applies only to a REVOKED or SUSPENDED certificate via a disciplinary hearing -- not an ordinary missed-renewal lapse.
records.penalty_cpe_notes: No extra CPE beyond the standard 120 credits over the prior 3 years already required for normal renewal (061-5 Wyo. Code R. Sec5-6).
records.lapse_trigger: All certificates expire December 31 each year. Failing to complete online renewal (fee + CPE compliance) by that date moves the certificate to expired status effective the new year, automatically -- no separate grace period is specified. Reactivating within 120 days of expiration additionally triggers a $150 CPE Extension Processing Fee.
records.citation: 061-3 Wyo. Code R. Sec3-6 (Renewal); fee at 061-1 Wyo. Code R. Sec1-13; reactivation CPE at 061-5 Wyo. Code R. Sec5-6
